title: Identify the water pressure regulator before changing the screw
description: Find the bell-shaped pressure reducing valve, measure pressure, and route high, low, or unstable pressure without guessing from symptoms alone.
prompt: What brought you to the regulator?
answer: A pressure regulator controls downstream pressure; it is not a backflow preventer. The first useful evidence is a gauge reading, the affected fixtures, and the exact model.
urgency: Do not make repeated blind adjustments. Very high pressure, active leakage, or a closed-system thermal expansion problem can damage plumbing.
diagramAlt: Water pressure regulator showing inlet, outlet, bell housing, adjustment bolt, and gauge point
identifiers: Usually installed near the water service entry after the main shutoff.
Often has an arrow on the body and a bell or dome over the spring.
An adjustment bolt changes the set point only within the model's documented range.

choices.label: Pressure seems too high
choices.detail: Confirm with a static gauge and check for overnight pressure rise.

choices.label: Pressure drops when water runs
choices.detail: Compare static and flowing PSI before replacing the valve.

choices.label: The regulator is leaking
choices.detail: The exact leak point separates a fitting issue from body or bell failure.

choices.label: I am planning replacement
choices.detail: Match size, pressure range, unions, access, and thermal expansion consequences.

steps.title: Confirm the device
steps.body: Record the body arrow, make, model, pipe size, and connection type.

steps.title: Measure before adjusting
steps.body: Take static and flowing readings at a reliable hose-thread gauge point.

steps.title: Choose adjust, service, or replace
steps.body: Use the model instructions and the reading pattern rather than a generic turn count.

safeChecks: Check multiple fixtures for the same symptom.
Record static, flowing, and overnight peak pressure.
stopConditions: Water leaks from the body or bell housing
The main shutoff or isolation plan is uncertain
Pressure changes accompany water-heater relief discharge
notThisDevice: A backflow assembly normally has test cocks and separate checks.
A thermal expansion tank is not a pressure regulator.
A sewer backwater valve is on drainage piping.
evidenceNote: Manufacturer instructions control adjustment and service. Local plumbing rules and the actual system pressure control the final decision.
